value.body: A science degree in living systems. Depending on the college it is offered as Zoology, Botany, Microbiology, Biotechnology, Biochemistry or a combined Life Sciences major. You study cell and molecular biology, genetics, physiology, ecology and lab techniques. It leads to biotech and pharma labs, research, healthcare-adjacent work and teaching.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in the science stream, usually with Biology (Physics, Chemistry and Biology). Central universities (Delhi University, BHU and others) admit through CUET-UG scores in the relevant subjects; many state universities and their colleges admit on Class 12 merit or a state test. You usually choose the major — or a combination of two or three subjects — at admission. This is a separate route from NEET-based medical admissions.

value.title: At a glance
items: Lab, research and biotech R&D roles commonly expect an M.Sc or PhD.
IIT JAM (Biotechnology paper), GAT-B (for biotechnology programmes) and CUET-PG lead to master's seats.
Entry roles include lab technician, quality control, clinical research and healthcare operations.
Teaching needs a B.Ed for schools, or a master's plus NET/SET or PhD for colleges.
